narrative:
The model estimates a 68% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors about your situation.

The strongest influence is that you have received other job opportunities while working here. Having external offers is a major signal that you may be considering leaving, and this factor pushed the prediction most strongly toward departure.

Next, your 6 to 10 years of experience in this organization actually worked in your favor. Most employees predicted to stay have shorter tenures of 1 to 5 years, so your longer time here slightly pulled the prediction back toward staying. However, this positive effect was not enough to outweigh the other influences.

The third most important factor is your overall 11 or more years of professional experience across all jobs. While many employees predicted to stay have only 1 to 5 years total experience, your extensive background also contributed toward the prediction that you might leave.

Taken together, these elements led the model to conclude you are more likely to depart than to remain. The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly, explore whether the external opportunities can be matched internally, and address any unmet needs around recognition or growth that may be encouraging you to look elsewhere. You may also want to reflect on what would make you want to stay long-term.
